sources.name: Man Group
sources.description: Multi-strategy: macro, quant, credit. Known for AHL systematic trading.

sources.name: Bridgewater Associates
sources.description: World's largest hedge fund. Macro, risk parity, All Weather strategy.

sources.name: AQR Capital Management
sources.description: Quantitative investing pioneer. Factor investing, alternatives, tax-aware.

sources.name: GMO LLC
sources.description: Value-oriented, contrarian. Famous for bubble calls and 7-Year forecasts.

sources.name: Oaktree Capital Management
sources.description: Credit/distressed debt specialist. Howard Marks memos are legendary.

sources.name: ARK Invest
sources.description: Disruptive innovation investing. AI, genomics, fintech, space, energy.

sources.name: Cambridge Associates
sources.description: Institutional investment advisor. Private equity, venture capital, endowment strategies.

sources.name: Wellington Management
sources.description: One of the world's largest private investment firms. Equity, fixed income, multi-asset, alternatives.

sources.name: Amundi Research Center
sources.description: Europe's largest asset manager. Macro, capital markets, ESG, fixed income, emerging markets.

sources.name: T. Rowe Price
sources.description: Active management specialist. Equity, fixed income, multi-asset. Strong fundamental research culture.

sources.name: PIMCO
sources.description: World's largest fixed-income manager. Macro forecasting, credit, rates, secular outlook.

sources.name: Aberdeen Investments
sources.description: UK-headquartered global asset manager. EM debt, multi-asset, sustainable investing.

sources.name: Brookfield Asset Management
sources.description: Global alternative asset manager. Real assets, infrastructure, renewables, private credit, private equity.

sources.name: J.P. Morgan Asset Management
sources.description: Investment management arm of J.P. Morgan. On the Minds of Investors series — market commentary across macro, equity, fixed income, alternatives.

sources.name: Verdad Capital
sources.description: Boston-based quantitative value investor. Empirical research on private equity, leveraged microcaps, factor investing, and capital efficiency.

sources.name: MSCI Research
sources.description: Index, factor and ESG analytics provider; ACWI/EAFE/EM benchmarks tracked by $16.5T+. Factor models (Quality/Value/Momentum), climate risk, multi-asset risk modelling.

sources.name: Natixis Investment Managers
sources.description: European multi-affiliate platform — 15+ boutiques (Loomis Sayles, Harris Associates, Mirova). Fixed income, value equity, ESG/climate, multi-asset. Tactical Take macro podcast.

sources.name: Apollo Global Management
sources.description: Largest US private credit / alts platform (~$1.03T). Pioneered ABF (asset-backed finance); private equity, real estate, insurance-solutions via Athene merger. Macro commentary from Marc Rowan and Torsten Slok.

sources.name: KKR
sources.description: Global alternatives leader (~$758B AUM). Buyout-pioneer firm founded 1976; covers private equity, infrastructure, real estate, private credit. Insights produced by Global Macro & Asset Allocation (GMAA) team.

sources.name: Janus Henderson Investors
sources.description: Active asset manager (~$480B AUM; take-private pending). Equity, fixed income, multi-asset and alternatives. Insights covers macro, geopolitics, AI and sector-level equity/credit analysis.

sources.name: Research Affiliates
sources.description: Quantitative investment firm founded by Rob Arnott (2002). Pioneered RAFI Fundamental Indexation — weights stocks by economic size (sales/cash flow/book/dividends) rather than market cap. Smart beta, factor investing, capital-market assumptions licensed to ~$159B of strategies.

sources.name: Goldman Sachs Asset Management
sources.description: One of the world's largest asset managers (~$3.3T AUM) across public and private markets. Multi-asset, equity, fixed income, alternatives and liquidity solutions for institutions and advisors; Insights publishes macro outlooks, market commentary and strategy notes.

sources.name: Robeco
sources.description: Dutch asset manager (~€200B AUM) headquartered in Rotterdam, founded 1929. Pioneer in quantitative equity investing and sustainable/ESG integration since the 1990s. Strong franchises in emerging-markets equity, global credit and factor-based strategies; Insights publishes quant research, ESG/climate analysis and EM/macro commentary.

sources.name: D. E. Shaw
sources.description: Quantitative multi-strategy hedge fund (~$65B AUM) founded 1988 by David E. Shaw. Pioneer of systematic/statistical-arbitrage investing with strong technology and computational-science DNA; trades across global equities, macro, credit, convertibles and private capital. Library publishes long-form research on portfolio construction, market microstructure and applied quant techniques.

sources.name: PineBridge Investments
sources.description: Global asset manager (~$100B AUM) headquartered in New York with deep Asia-Pacific roots; originated as AIG Investments (1996), spun out under Pacific Century Group in 2010 and acquired by MetLife Investment Management (completed Dec 2025). Specializes in fixed income (EM debt, leveraged finance, IG bonds), multi-asset and active equities; widely followed publications include Capital Market Line (5-year capital-market assumptions) and Investment Strategy Insights (weekly macro/positioning).

sources.name: Ares Management
sources.description: Leading global alternative investment manager (~$620B AUM) specializing in private credit, private equity, real assets and infrastructure. Founded in 1997, listed on NYSE (ARES). Direct-lending pioneer with one of the largest US middle-market credit platforms; significant insurance solutions business via Aspida.

sources.name: Matthews Asia
sources.description: Asia- and emerging-markets equity specialist (~$6.6B AUM), founded 1991 and privately owned, with offices in San Francisco and Hong Kong. Active, bottom-up fundamental investing across Asian and EM equities — China, India, Japan and broader emerging markets — spanning all-cap growth, dividend, small-cap and innovation strategies plus a more recent active-ETF lineup.

sources.name: Capital Group (Capital Ideas)
sources.description: One of the world's largest active asset managers (~$3.3T AUM), founded 1931 and home to the American Funds. Known for 'The Capital System' — several portfolio managers independently run sleeves of each fund — and a long-horizon, fundamental, active approach spanning global equity, fixed income and multi-asset strategies.

sources.name: Acadian Asset Management
sources.description: Quantitative, systematic investment manager (~$120B AUM), founded 1986 and headquartered in Boston. Pioneered factor-based, bottom-up equity investing — systematically scoring thousands of stocks worldwide on valuation, quality, growth and sentiment signals — across global, international, emerging- and frontier-markets mandates, and extends the same model-driven process to systematic credit and multi-asset strategies.
